# Adjudication Task — Chapter 502

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃502화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|“여기 있었군.”
  6|
  7|등 뒤에서 불현듯 들려온 누군가의 목소리에, 가부좌를 튼 채 눈을 감고 있던 노인의 미간이 꿈틀거렸다.
  8|
  9|“따로 누군가를 초대한 기억은 없거늘.”
 10|
 11|“알 바 아니지. 그나저나 생각 이상으로 좁군. 터무니없을 정도야.”
 12|
 13|“좁을 수밖에. 불청객을 위한 자리는 마련해 두지 않았으니.”
 14|
 15|“칠 주야 전쯤이던가. 분명 누군가에게 비슷한 말을 했던 것 같은데…….”
 16|
 17|어째서일까. 그 말이 들려온 순간 노인의 작은 등이 움찔 떨렸다.
 18|
 19|그러나 초대받지 않은 불청객이 그 이유에 대해 생각하기도 전에, 예리하게 날 선 목소리가 날아들었다.
 20|
 21|“떠나라. 수련에 방해되니.”
 22|
 23|“그 수련 계속하도록. 내 친히 호법(護法)을 서 주지.”
 24|
 25|노인, 화왕 적천강은 감았던 눈을 떴다.
 26|
 27|어둠이 사라지고 군데군데 이끼가 낀 축축한 동굴의 벽면이 시야를 가득 채운다.
 28|
 29|이어 굳게 다물어져 있던 입술 사이로 성마른 목소리가 흘러나왔다.
 30|
 31|“다른 누구도 아닌 살성(殺星)에게 호법을 맡기라니. 웃기지도 않는 농을 지껄이는구나.”
 32|
 33|“아끼는 제자에 비하면 늙은 목숨 정도는 맡길 수 있을 것 같은데. 내가 착각한 건가?”
 34|
 35|“……!”
 36|
 37|그 한마디에 적천강의 눈꺼풀이 파르르 떨렸다. 그리고 다음 순간.
 38|
 39|스으윽.
 40|
 41|가부좌를 튼 채 앉아 있던 자그마한 체구가 허공에 떠올라 천천히 뒤돌아 착지했다.
 42|
 43|비좁은 동굴 입구를 가로막은 한 사람을 말없이 바라보던 적천강이 문득 입을 열었다.
 44|
 45|“노부가 여기 있는지는 어찌 알았지?”
 46|
 47|문경이 건조한 목소리로 대답했다.
 48|
 49|“올라와 보니 웬 대호 한 마리가 다가와 머리를 부비더군. 한두 번 해 본 솜씨가 아니었어.”
 50|
 51|“족적을 남기지 않았거늘.”
 52|
 53|“본래 하던 일이 그쪽이라.”
 54|
 55|“제아무리 의생 흉내를 내도 결국 살수다, 이건가?”
 56|
 57|“잊으려 해도 잊히지 않는 것들이 있지. 그뿐이다. 수많은 이목이 깔려 있고 주위에는 온통 강물뿐. 갈 만한 곳은 뻔하지.”
 58|
 59|뛰어난 대장장이가 벼린 검은 세월이 흘러도 날이 무뎌지지 않는 법.
 60|
 61|살성이라는 이름의 명검이 지닌 예리함은 사십여 년의 세월이 흐른 지금에도 여전했다.
 62|
 63|아니, 살수로서의 본능은 떨어졌을지 몰라도 무인으로서의 경지는 오히려 높아졌다.
 64|
 65|“……더 은밀한 곳을 찾았어야 했나.”
 66|
 67|“그랬다면 시간이 조금 더 걸렸겠지.”
 68|
 69|살수는 암살과 추격의 달인이다.
 70|
 71|담담한 문경의 표정에서 자신감을 읽어 낸 적천강이 중얼거렸다.
 72|
 73|“염병할. 재수 없는 살수 놈이로고.”
 74|
 75|“다 들린다.”
 76|
 77|“들으라고 한 소리니라.”
 78|
 79|“다짜고짜 욕을 하다니. 참으로 성질머리가 고약한 주인이군.”
 80|
 81|“다짜고짜 면벽수련(面壁修練) 중에 찾아온 놈만 할까.”
 82|
 83|“천하의 화왕이 면벽수련이라.”
 84|
 85|고저 없는 목소리가 동굴 안을 울렸다.
 86|
 87|낮게 뇌까린 문경의 시선이 천천히 주위를 훑었다. 동굴이라 부르기 민망할 정도로 비좁고 축축한 그곳에는 가부좌를 튼 노인을 제외하면 그 어떤 것도 존재하지 않았다.
 88|
 89|그리고, 오직 하나뿐이라 더욱 잘 보이는 것들이 있었다.
 90|
 91|‘적천강. 이자가…….’
 92|
 93|갈라진 입술과 살가죽 위로 도드라진 뼈마디. 적천강의 상태를 놓치지 않고 포착해 낸 문경의 눈빛이 가라앉았다.
 94|
 95|그의 비쩍 마른 몰골을 보아하니, 칠주야 동안 곡기는커녕 물 한 방울 입에 대지 않았음이 분명했다.
 96|
 97|제아무리 초절정 고수라고는 하나 몸에 무리가 가는 일인 것은 명백하다.
 98|
 99|“미련한 짓을 하는군.”
100|
101|문경의 말에 담긴 의미를 못 알아차릴 적천강이 아니었다. 움푹 들어간 눈가에서 형형한 안광이 빛났다.
102|
103|“네놈이 아까 했던 말 그대로 돌려주지. 알 바 아니다.”
104|
105|“벽곡단은?”
106|
107|“안 먹는다. 맛대가리 없어서.”
108|
109|“……그것까지 닮은 건가.”
110|
111|“뭐라?”
112|
113|“아니다. 아무것도.”
114|
115|쓸모없는 이야기를 해 버렸다. 단지 벽곡단이 맛없어서 먹지 않았다는 적천강의 어설픈 이유만큼이나.
116|
117|고개를 내저은 문경이 말을 이었다.
118|
119|“의생으로서 충고하건대, 좋은 선택이 아니라고 말해 주지.”
120|
121|“노부로서 말하는데, 신경 꺼라.”
122|
123|“생각 이상으로 고집불통이로군.”
124|
125|“네놈은 생각 이상으로 참견이 심하구나. 언제부터 남의 일에 그리 신경 썼느냐?”
126|
127|“그건…….”
128|
129|문경은 문득 입을 다물었다. 뭐라 반박하고 싶었지만, 딱히 할 말이 떠오르지 않았다.
130|
131|그리고 그것은 그 스스로도 적천강의 말을 인정했다는 뜻이나 마찬가지였다.
132|
133|‘썩 틀린 말은 아닌 셈인가.’
134|
135|처음 사천을 떠날 때만 해도 이러지는 않았다. 그러나 분명 그는 언제부터인가 조금씩 달라지기 시작했다.
136|
137|다른 이들의 이목을 속이기 위해 순진무구한 소년 의생으로 지낼 때는 웃기도 하고 말도 많았지만, 적천강이나 진태경과 단둘이 있을 때는 굳이 어울리지도 않는 연기를 할 필요가 없었다.
138|
139|그런데 어째서일까. 오늘따라 말이 많아진 기분이다.
140|
141|아니, 어쩌면 그것은 비단 오늘만의 일이 아닐 것이다.
142|
143|‘도대체 왜.’
144|
145|문경은 칠주야 전, 적천강의 말도 안 되는 제안을 받아들이던 그때의 자신을 떠올렸다.
146|
147|형용할 수 없을 만큼 씁쓸한 표정으로 말을 이어 가던 적천강의 얼굴 또한 함께.
148|
149|굳게 다물어져 있던 문경의 입술이 열린 것은 바로 그때였다.
150|
151|“왜 묻지 않지?”
152|
153|“무엇을 말이냐.”
154|
155|“진태경에 관해서.”
156|
157|“……!”
158|
159|이번에는 적천강의 말문이 막혔다.
160|
161|애써 피하고자 했던 그 이름.
162|
163|문경이 모르는 척 지나쳐 주길 바랐던 한 사람의 이름은 억지로 가라앉혔던 마음에 파문을 일으키기에 충분했다.
164|
165|“녀석은…… 잘하고 있나?”
166|
167|“그럭저럭 따라오고 있다. 나쁘지 않아.”
168|
169|적천강은 참지 못하고 헛웃음을 터트렸다.
170|
171|“왜 웃지?”
172|
173|“헛소리라는 걸 아니까. 그럭저럭이라니. 노부가 근래 들은 말 중에 가장 재미있군.”
174|
175|“…….”
176|
177|“노부는 신경 쓰지 말고 본심을 이야기해라.”
178|
179|적천강을 물끄러미 바라보던 문경이 입을 열었다.
180|
181|“성취가 대단히 빠르다. 나조차도 놀랄 만큼.”
182|
183|“본심을 이야기하라고 했을 터.”
184|
185|“이것이 내 본심이다.”
186|
187|“반쪽짜리 본심이지. 탐난다는 말이 빠졌으니.”
188|
189|“…….”
190|
191|“그래, 항상 그랬지.”
192|
193|적천강은 희미한 웃음을 머금었다.
194|
195|진태경을 처음 만났던 그 날부터 지금까지. 하루하루가 놀라움의 연속이었다.
196|
197|하늘이 내린 근골에 뛰어난 무재. 자신만의 무공을 정립한 초절정 고수라면 누구인들 제자로 탐내지 않을 수 없을 것이다.
198|
199|그리고 그건 적천강 본인에게도 해당하는 말이었다.
200|
201|“처음 태경이 그 녀석을 알게 되었을 때, 문득 그런 생각이 들었지. 이 아이에게 열화문의 무공이 이어진다면 무(武)의 끝자락을 볼 수 있지 않을까, 하는.”
202|
203|수백 년간 내려온 열화문의 명맥을 잇기 위해서는 인재가 필요했고, 진태경은 그 기준에 누구보다 부합하는 유일한 사람이었다.
204|
205|분명히 그랬다. 첫 시작은.
206|
207|“처음에는 그저 놀라웠고, 그다음은 안타까웠다. 노부에게 허락된 시간은 그리 많지 않았으니까.”
208|
209|단신으로 천 명의 마교도를 쓰러트리고, 숱한 마두를 무릎 꿇렸다.
210|
211|강대한 일신의 무위로 전장의 판도를 뒤집으며 정마대전의 승리를 선봉에서 이끈 그였다.
212|
213|그러나 화왕(火王)이라 불리며 천하 무림의 우러름을 받던 초절정 고수의 진정한 적은 따로 있었다.
214|
215|“오래전의 일이야. 심마(心魔)가 찾아온 것은.”
216|
217|첫 제자가 남기고 간 상처는 깊었고, 이내 홀로 남겨진 스승의 몸과 마음을 갉아먹었다. 조금씩, 천천히. 하지만 계속해서.
218|
219|“이상한 일이었지. 모든 것이 계속해서 앞으로 나아가는데, 노부는 홀로 뒷걸음질 치고 있었어.”
220|
221|세월은 쏘아진 화살처럼 빨랐다. 화살촉이 표적에 닿았을 때는 이미 삼십여 년이라는 시간이 흐른 뒤였다.
222|
223|그 어떤 깨달음조차 얻지 못하고 시간만을 강물에 흘려보낸 적천강은 어느 날 믿기 힘든 현실과 마주했다.
224|
225|“푸른 날이었다. 시원한 바람을 맞다가 문득 정신을 차려 보니 사람들 속이었지. 노부도 모르는 시간 속에서 한나절이 지나 버린 게야. 허허.”
226|
227|노환(老患)이 찾아왔던 그날도 이렇게 웃었었다.
228|
229|기뻐서도 아니었고 허탈해서도 아니었다. 어찌해야 할지 몰라 그저 웃었다.
230|
231|적천강이 자신이 해야 할 일을 깨달은 것은 처음의 한나절이 이틀이 된 직후였다.
232|
233|“한 사람을 죽이기 위해 구화산을 떠났다.”
234|
235|그리고 한 사람을 얻어 돌아왔다.
236|
237|“노부의 첫 제자였지. 더 늦기 전에 이 손으로 직접 처리해야 했어.”
238|
239|하지만 진태경을 만난 뒤 깨달았다. 자신이 늦은 것은 그뿐만이 아니었다는 것을.
240|
241|“살성. 자네에게 다시 한번 부탁해도 되겠나.”
242|
243|문경을 향한 적천강의 뒤바뀐 눈빛과 어조는 그 어느 때보다 부드러웠다.
244|
245|“혹여 노부가 없을 때, 그 아이의 든든한 그늘막이 되어 달라고. 새로운 스승이 되어 달라고 말일세.”
246|
247|주름 하나 없는 매끈한 이마에 깊은 골이 새겨졌다. 문경은 미간을 좁힌 채 적천강을 응시했다.
248|
249|“지금 한 그 말, 진심인가?”
250|
251|“그 어느 때보다.”
252|
253|“도대체 왜?”
254|
255|“말했던 그대로일세. 이제 시간이 없어.”
256|
257|“이 무슨…….”
258|
259|난데없이 새로운 스승이 되어 달라니. 시간이 없다니.
260|
261|적천강이 어떤 상태인지 알고 있는 문경으로서는 쉽사리 이해가 되지 않았다.
262|
263|모든 것의 원천이라 할 수 있는 선천지기가 흐트러졌으니 서서히 힘을 잃겠지만, 그것은 수년이 흐른 뒤에야 벌어질 일이었다. 이건, 너무 이르다.
264|
265|“내 이리 청하네.”
266|
267|“……!”
268|
269|이제는 고개마저 숙인다. 다른 누구도 아닌 바로 그 화왕 적천강이.
270|
271|무림의 그 누구도 보지 못했을 광경을 마주한 문경은 당혹스러움마저 느낄 지경이었다.
272|
273|“대체 이유가 뭐지? 분명 칠주야 전만 하더라도…….”
274|
275|이어지려던 문경의 목소리가 뚝 끊겼다. 말을 삼킨 그는 어느새 파문이 일고 있는 적천강의 눈동자를 말없이 응시했다.
276|
277|그리고 순간 내려앉은 숨 막히는 침묵 속에서, 문경의 뇌리에 한 줄기 생각이 스쳤다.
278|
279|‘그랬군. 그리된 거였어.’
280|
281|그의 생각이 맞는다면 모든 의문이 풀린다.
282|
283|적천강이 왜 이리도 과한 걱정을 하는지. 진태경을 포함한 다른 이들에게서 모습을 감추었는지.
284|
285|또 대화 도중 보이는 이상한 반응들이 어디에서 나오는지.
286|
287|문경은 탄식처럼 내뱉었다.
288|
289|“칠주야 전이…… 아니었군.”
290|

“I said to tell me what you really think.”

[P80]
“That *is* what I think.”

[P81]
“Half of it. You left out the part where you want him for yourself.”

[P82]
“…”

[P83]
“Yes. It was always like that.”

[P84]
A faint smile touched Jeok Cheongang’s lips.

[P85]
From the day he first met Jin Taekyung, every day had brought a new surprise. With a Heaven-given physique and extraordinary martial talent, Taekyung was someone any Supreme Peak master who had established martial arts of his own would want as a Disciple.

[P86]
Jeok Cheongang was no exception.

[P87]
“When I first got to know Taekyung, a thought struck me. If I passed the Fire Gate Clan’s martial arts on to this boy, perhaps he might see the very limits of martial arts.”

[P88]
The Fire Gate Clan needed someone to carry on a lineage hundreds of years old, and Jin Taekyung fit that need better than anyone else.

[P89]
That was how it had started.

[P90]
“At first, I was simply amazed. Then I felt regret. I didn’t have much time left.”

[P91]
Alone, he had defeated a thousand Demonic Cult martial artists and brought countless fiends to their knees. By the strength of his own martial arts, he had turned the tide of battle and led the charge toward victory in the Great Faction War.

[P92]
Yet the Supreme Peak master revered throughout Murim as the Fire King had another, truer enemy.

[P93]
“It was long ago that the Heart Demon came for me.”

[P94]
The wound left by his first Disciple ran deep. It ate away at the body and mind of the Master left alone. Little by little, slowly, without ever stopping.

[P95]
“It was strange. Everything else kept moving forward, while I alone was walking backward.”

[P96]
The years flew like an arrow. By the time it struck its target, more than thirty had passed.

[P97]
Jeok Cheongang had let them flow downriver without gaining the slightest enlightenment. Then, one day, he came face-to-face with something he could scarcely believe.

[P98]
“It was a clear blue day. I was enjoying the cool breeze, and then I came to my senses among a crowd of people. Half a day had passed, and I knew nothing of it. Heh.”

[P99]
He had laughed like that on the day the infirmities of old age first came upon him.

[P100]
Not out of happiness or resignation. He had laughed because he didn’t know what else to do.

[P101]
It was only when that first lost half-day became two full days that Jeok Cheongang knew what he had to do.

[P102]
“I left Mount Jiuhua to kill one person.”

[P103]
And returned with one person.

[P104]
“He was my first Disciple. I had to deal with him myself before it was too late.”

[P105]
After meeting Jin Taekyung, though, Jeok Cheongang had realized that wasn’t the only thing he had left too late.

[P106]
“Slaughter Saint. May I ask you for another favor?”

[P107]
His gaze and tone had changed. Both were gentler than Mungyeong had ever known them.

[P108]
“If I’m no longer here, be a shelter for that boy. Be his new Master.”

[P109]
A deep furrow formed on Mungyeong’s smooth forehead. He stared at Jeok Cheongang through narrowed eyes.

[P110]
“Do you mean that?”

[P111]
“More than anything.”

[P112]
“Why?”

[P113]
“Just as I said. I have no time left.”

[P114]
“What are you…”

[P115]
A new Master, out of nowhere? No time left?

[P116]
Mungyeong knew Jeok Cheongang’s condition, but he couldn’t make sense of this. His innate qi, the source of everything, had been disrupted. He would gradually lose his strength, but that should have taken years.

[P117]
This was too soon.

[P118]
“I ask this of you.”

[P119]
“…!”

[P120]
Jeok Cheongang bowed his head. The Fire King himself.

[P121]
Faced with a sight no one else in Murim had likely ever seen, Mungyeong was at a loss.

[P122]
“Why? Seven days and nights ago, you were clearly…”

[P123]
His voice stopped. He swallowed the rest and stared at the disturbance in Jeok Cheongang’s eyes.

[P124]
A thought struck him in the suffocating silence.

[P125]
*So that’s it. That’s what happened.*

[P126]
If he was right, it explained everything: Jeok Cheongang’s excessive worry, his disappearance from Jin Taekyung and the others, and his strange reactions throughout their conversation.

[P127]
Mungyeong spoke on a sigh. “It wasn’t seven days and nights ago, was it?”

[P128]
“No. It was seven days and nights.”

[P129]
Jeok Cheongang smiled bitterly.

[P130]
“But to me, those seven days and nights were only five days.”

[P131]
Time flowed equally for everyone. Not everyone experienced it equally.

[P132]
The first uninvited guest, arriving a step ahead of Mungyeong, had been the infirmities of old age. They had stolen two days from Jeok Cheongang and fled.

[P133]
“…When did it start?”

[P134]
“Sichuan.”

[P135]
“Sichuan? But when I took your pulse, you were clearly…”

[P136]
“The symptoms appeared just after we left Sichuan. After that, I took care to avoid you.”

[P137]
Why had he hidden it? Why?

[P138]
The question died on Mungyeong’s tongue. He already knew.

[P139]
He knew how small a person could feel on realizing he had grown old. How frightening it was to discover that the infirmities of old age were making his mind come and go.

[P140]
Seeing Mungyeong fall silent, Jeok Cheongang gave a rueful smile.

[P141]
“Even if I’d come to tell you, nothing would have changed. I know my own body. You may be the Divine Physician, with medical skill that reaches Heaven, but even you can’t stop innate qi once it starts leaking away.”

[P142]
“…”

[P143]
“At first, my memory grew hazy. Then one day, moments were missing from my day. I knew what it meant because I’d been through it before.”

[P144]
Those moments became the time it took to drink a cup of tea. That became fifteen minutes. Now it was two days.

[P145]
Jeok Cheongang had searched desperately for a way to stop it, to no avail.

[P146]
“Acquired qi from elixirs can’t restore a balance that’s already been broken. That left me one choice.”

[P147]
“…Enlightenment.”

[P148]
“Yes. Enlightenment.”

[P149]
“So that’s why you began this secluded meditation.”

[P150]
“I wanted to live as Jeok Cheongang, the Fire King. Not as an old man who couldn’t remember his own name, but as the current Sect Leader of the Fire Gate Clan and someone’s Master.”

[P151]
His desolate voice echoed through the cave. Drops gathered on the damp ceiling and fell, like an old man’s tears.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). **Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.

- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.

## Critical binding translation rules

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.
- Search only exact Korean terms already present in the current chapter; the compendium contains future-sensitive entries.
- Never re-romanize established names or invent grand names for uncertain terms. First use of an unlisted name or title almost always needs a footnote or a mapped ledger term.
- Use `qi` for Murim energy and `mana` for the modern Hunter system when the source distinguishes them. Preserve an established chapter-specific rendering such as `internal energy` when the exact glossary and surrounding Korean distinguish accumulated `공력` from resulting `기운`.
- In System panels, render `등급` as `**Grade:**` for quest, item, skill, and martial-art classifications. Reserve `rank` for Hunter classifications or ordinary prose; never replace a System `Grade` field with `Rank`.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

## Footnotes

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

## Spoilers and Scope

- Safe profiles contain only facts revealed through the latest completed chapter.
- Never read `characters/spoilers/` during drafting. Reviewers may consult one relevant sealed profile only for a specific unresolved continuity issue after the draft is complete.
- Future knowledge may prevent contradiction but may not add early names, pronouns, certainty, motives, or foreshadowing.
- Translate exactly one requested chapter unless the user explicitly requests a batch. Never modify Korean source files under `source/`.
